accuracy.evidence: Definitions match the DfE 2013 Year 6 geometry statement and its non-statutory notes: radius as centre-to-edge segment and length, diameter as a chord through the centre (the longest chord) with d = 2r, circumference as the distance round the edge, radii as the plural. The roll scene uses C = πd for the drawn distance (d = 2, 3, 4 cm give 6.3, 9.4 and 12.6 cm), described only as 'a bit more than 3 diameters' so pi is left to the next topic; m5 gives about 157 cm for a 50 cm wheel (π × 50 = 157.08). The chord-length readout in the diameter scene is 2r·sin(θ/2), so it peaks exactly at 2r when B is opposite A. Parameterised answers 2*a and a are whole numbers at every corner of their ranges.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips in NCETM's Year 6 circle guidance and common KS2 errors: any line across is a diameter (decoy chord in every naming round, robot claim 3, p3, m6, challenge tags 'across' and 'radline'), diameter is half the radius / converting the wrong way (prediction 2 offers 1.5 cm, robot claim 2, challenge 'half' and 'double'), compasses set to the diameter (compass scene message when the opening equals the diameter, robot claim 5, p4, challenge 'compass'), radii in different directions differ (prediction 1, m3) and circumference read as the width or the inside (p5, challenge 'width' and 'inside').

lab_distinct.evidence: Every scene is about this topic's own geometry: hit-testing the centre, three lettered segments and the ring; a handle constrained to the circle so the radius readout never changes; point B constrained to the circle with a live chord length that peaks at the diameter; a pair of compasses whose opening is set on a ruler and draws a circle of that radius next to a dashed target; a wheel that rolls with rotation s/r and lays diameter rods under the track. flagchord (lesson 130) handles chords, arcs, sectors and tangents for ages 14+. The lab_distinct gate keeps flag_circp.js under 30% similar to every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the rules by doing: the radius readout stays at 4 cm at all three rings while a dashed copy of each radius is left behind; the A-to-B readout climbs (for r = 4.5 it passes 8.9 cm) and the round only completes when the line passes through the centre, with the message giving 2 × r; a wrong compass setting draws a circle that is visibly twice or half the dashed target, with the size stated; one wheel turn leaves a red line that the blue diameter rods cover three times with a small orange piece left over.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Is a radius pointing up the same length as one pointing sideways?' (tempting: it depends on direction; the readout stays 4 cm at every ring), 'Radius 3 cm, how long is the diameter?' (tempting: 1.5 cm from halving; the first circle's diameter comes out 6 cm) and 'One turn covers about how many diameters?' (tempting: exactly 2 or exactly 4; the rods show 3 and a bit). Each step's completion message reveals the learner's own prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions, each with two wrong answers tagged to a slip, and nine distinct messages in CIRP.SLIP: half (you halved, so double), double (you doubled, so halve), same (radius and diameter are not equal), across (a diameter must pass through the centre), radline (a radius starts at the centre), compass (the opening is the radius), width (the circumference is longer than the width), inside (that is the area) and twice (one turn is more than 3 diameters). Each names the slip and gives the fix.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text uses short sentences, one idea each, and passes the FK limit; the adult text names the Year 6 statement and the key words and passes its limit. Canvas text is dark on white labels over a pale paper background, and every label shrinks to fit at 390 px (checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in both themes).

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs each teach one thing: the centre and equal distance, the radius, the diameter as two radii with a worked 4 cm to 8 cm example, and the circumference with the wheel. Adult paragraphs give the curriculum statement and key words, the formal definitions with d = 2r and why compasses use the radius, four named mistakes, and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler and under 12% overlap with every lesson, including lesson 130.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots (dark) and desktop (light) of every step at rest and part-way through Show me, plus a finished wheel roll and a wrong compass draw: the circle fills the canvas width with the lettered lines clear of each other, ring targets sit on the edge, the ruler runs 0 to 10 cm across the full width with labels readable, the rolled wheel's rods and summary fit under the track, and the buttons under the canvas wrap into two rows of 44 px targets.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Line A, Line B, Line C, The dot and The curved edge; turn buttons for the radius and point B in 15 degree steps (every target is reachable); Close, Open and Draw the circle; Roll a bit and Next wheel; Right and Slip. Lines are told apart by letter as well as colour. Every result goes through c.say and the canvas aria-label; challenge feedback is a polite live region. The walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
